items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to providing for
decommissioning oversight boards for nuclear power plants in New York state
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8154

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law, in relation to providing for
decommissioning oversight boards for nuclear power plants in New York
state

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this legislation is to establish the New York State
Decommissioning Oversight Boards for Nuclear Power Plants.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. A new section 174 is added to the Public Service Law, titled,
NEW YORK STATE DECOMMISSIONING OVERSIGHT BOARD. 1. Defines the following
terms are defined: retirement, retiring facility, decommissioning peri-
od, reuse, decommissioning activities, licensee, site, site restoration,
decommissioning trust fund, comments, spent nuclear fuel, spent fuel
management, community member. 2. Creates the New York State Decommis-
sioning Oversight Board or Boards (NYSDOB). a. Within one month after
the facility's future closure is noticed to the nuclear Regulatory
Commission (NRC), a NYSDOB shall be established. It shall be in place
till the decommissioning period is complete, all site restoration is
complete and released by all governmental authorities for reuse, and all
spent fuel has been removed. b. The NYSDOB shall ensure state and feder-
al regulations are followed, and report accordingly, as needed. The
NYSDOB shall supervise the disbursement of the retiring facility's
decommissioning trust fund, facilitate public involvement and transpar-
ency throughout the process, etc. c. Eleven 'agency members' will serve
on the NYSDOB. D. Seven to ten members will be appointed by the Gover-
nor. e. There are no term limits for the agency members, and appointed
members will serve staggered terms of three years. f. No person with
financial interest in any state nuclear plant may serve on the NYSDOB.
g. A vice chair will be selected by the NYSDOB, and be from the board,
with an initial term of one year, with subsequent terms being two years.
3. NYSDOB shall meet at least four times a year to monitor and discuss
the decommissioning trust fund, decommissioning activities, the manage-
ment of nuclear waste, etc. Once decommissioning activities are complete
the board may meet at least once a year. 4. Details the powers and
duties of the board. 5. Details of licensee requirements are detailed,
which include that the licensee shall complete decommissioning activ-
ities at the facility within forty years of retirement so that the site
can be returned to productive use. 6. Any funds remaining in the decom-
missioning trust fund shall revert to NYSERDA to be spent on renew- able
energy projects that benefit the service areas within which rate- payers
contributed to the decommissioning trust fund. 7. Board members receive
no salary but shall be compensated for reasonable travel expenses
exceeding two hundred miles. 8. Outlines how the NYSDOB will be adminis-
tered.

Section 2. Establishes the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

This section of this memorandum is not applicable at this time.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The New York State Decommissioning Oversight Board is vital to ensure
the proper decommissioning of nuclear power plants within our State.

The Vermont Nuclear Decommissioning Citizens Advisory Panel was put in
place to deal with the decommissioning of the Vermont Yankee Nuclear
Power Station, which was that State's only nuclear power plant.  Because
of this, they were able to use a more local approach. Being that New
York State has six nuclear reactors in three separate locations, a
stronger state-wide approach is warranted.  Presently, there are no
agencies with the expertise, resources and authority to effectively
oversee this complex process. This vital legislation would change that.

The decommissioning of nuclear power plants is new to the State of New
York, and it is important that the process runs smoothly. This board
will protect the financial, environmental and physical interests of our
residents while our nuclear power plants begin to seize operation and go
offline.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is new legislation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

There are no fiscal implications to our local governments. If there are
any fiscal implications to our State they will be minimal as they will
be to cover travel expenditures for attending over site meetings, which
is standard with most State task forces.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8154A

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law, in relation to providing for
decommissioning oversight boards for nuclear power plants in New York
state

The purpose of this legislation is to establish the New York State
Decommissioning Oversight Boards for Nuclear Power Plants.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. A new section 174 is added to the Public Service Law, titled,
NEW YORK STATE DECOMMISSIONING OVERSIGHT BOARD. 1. Defines relevant
terms. 2. Creates the New York State Decommissioning Oversight Board or
Boards (NYSDOB). a. Outlines timelines by which Boards are to be estab-
lished and requirements for Board dissolution.

b. The NYSDOB shall assess whether state and federal regulations are
followed, and report accordingly, as needed. The NYSDOB shall observe
the disbursement of the retiring facility's decommissioning trust fund,
and facilitate public involvement and transparency throughout the proc-
ess. c. Nine "agency members" will serve on the NYSDOB along with the
Attorney General and the State Comptroller. d. Six "appointed members"
will be appointed by the Governor, and the temporary president of the
Senate and speaker of the Assembly shall each appoint two members.
e.There are no term limits for the agency members, and appointed members
will serve staggered terms of three years. f. No person with financial
interest in any nuclear plant may serve on the NYSDOB. g. A vice chair
will be selected by the NYSDOB, and be from the board, with an initial
term of one year, with subsequent terms being two years.

3. NYSDOB shall meet at least four times each year to monitor and
discuss the decommissioning trust fund, decommissioning activities, the
management of nuclear waste, etc. Once decommissioning activities are
complete the NYSDOB shall meet at least once per year.

4. Details the powers and duties of the board. 5. Licensee requirements
are detailed. 6. Any funds remaining in the decommissioning trust fund
shall revert to NYSERDA to be spent on renewable energy systems that
benefit the service areas within which ratepayers contributed to the
decommissioning trust fund. 7. Board members receive no salary but shall
be compensated for actual and necessary expenses incurred in the
performance of their duties. 8. Outlines how the NYSDOB will be adminis-
tered.

Section 2. Establishes the effective date.

5. The "A" print also removed a requirement that the facility be
released for reuse within 40 years of commencing decommissioning activ-
ities, and clarifies that communications between the licensee and the
NRC are to be provided to the board as soon as practicable.
